topics.label: Introduction and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture on cancer causes and establishes its objectives.

topics.label: Cancer evolution and the origins of cancer-driving mutations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain cancer development through clonal evolution driven by mutations arising from different sources.

topics.label: Evidence and debate about environmental cancer risks
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the evidence used to attribute cancer risk to environmental influences.

topics.label: Infectious causes of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infectious agents contribute to cancer development, with Burkitt lymphoma as a specific example.

topics.label: Carcinogen-induced DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how carcinogenic exposures produce DNA damage through mechanisms that can depend on metabolic activation and tissue location.

topics.label: Tumour initiation, promotion and tissue susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how carcinogenesis progresses through initiation and promotion in tissues whose susceptibility depends on their biological context.

topics.label: Human evidence of carcinogen exposure and carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how biological evidence from people supports the assessment of carcinogen exposure and cancer risk.

topics.label: Experimental carcinogenicity testing and its limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics assess laboratory tests used to identify carcinogenic potential and the limitations of interpreting their results.

topics.label: Lecture summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This closing consolidates the lecture's findings on environmental cancer risks and carcinogenicity assessment in relation to risk–benefit decisions.
